content:
The hemisphere has centre \(O\) at the origin and radius \(R=200\).  
The disk lies in the plane \(z=0\) and also has radius \(200\).

Place a sphere of radius \(r=42\) on the disk at a point \(P=(x,y,0)\).  
Its centre is then at  
\[
C=(x,y,r)=(x,y,42).
\]

For the small sphere to lie completely inside the hemisphere we need every point of the small sphere to be inside the large sphere of radius \(200\) centred at the origin (the hemisphere is the upper half of this sphere).  
The farthest point of the small sphere from the origin is at distance \(|OC|+r\), where \(|OC|=\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}+r^{2}}\).  
Thus we require  

\[
\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}+r^{2}}+r\le R .
\]

Substituting \(r=42\) and \(R=200\),

\[
\sqrt{x^{2}+y^{2}+42^{2}} \le 200-42 = 158,
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
x^{2}+y^{2}\le 158^{2}-42^{2}.
\]

Compute the right–hand side:

\[
158^{2}=24964,\qquad 42^{2}=1764,
\]
\[
158^{2}-42^{2}=24964-1764=23200.
\]

Hence the admissible points \(P\) form a circular region \(\mathcal T\) centred at the origin with radius \(\sqrt{23200}\).

The area of \(\mathcal T\) is \(\pi\cdot 23200\); the area of the whole disk is \(\pi\cdot 200^{2}= \pi\cdot 40000\).  

Therefore

\[
\frac{\text{area}(\mathcal T)}{\text{area of disk}}=
\frac{23200}{40000}= \frac{29}{50}.
\]

So \(p=29,\; q=50\) (which are relatively prime) and  

\[
p+q = 29+50 = 79.
\]

\[
\boxed{79}
\]
